contract: GET /feed/:slug/item/:episodeId/*. Serve one feed episode file without authentication by feed slug and episode id: Content-Type from the file extension (audio/mp4 for m4b/m4a, audio/mpeg for mp3, audio/flac for flac), Content-Length, Accept-Ranges bytes with 206/416 range answers and no attachment disposition. The path tail after the episode id is ignored, so the route never returns a file other than the stored episode. Unknown feed or episode answers 404. Closing the feed invalidates every enclosure URL.
exceptions: force is not applicable: no feed route has a force, hard or override mode; a feed is refreshed implicitly when its entity is newer than entityUpdatedAt.
Last-Modified/ETag/If-Range caching semantics are not asserted: clients read the enclosure through a feed reader, which is not part of this contract.
The episode path tail is deliberately not validated by upstream; the traversal case asserts only that the stored episode is served.

invariants.contract: GET /feed/:slug/item/:episodeId/media.m4b and .../media.mp3 with no token answer 200 with the exact bytes of the episode's persisted filePath, Content-Type audio/mp4 / audio/mpeg / audio/flac by extension, Content-Length equal to the file size, Accept-Ranges bytes, no Content-Disposition and no authentication. Closed byte ranges answer 206 with Content-Range and the exact slice, suffix ranges answer the file tail, and a range at the file size answers 416 with Content-Range bytes */<size> and no media bytes.

An unknown slug, an unknown episode id and an episode id belonging to another feed all answer 404 without any episode bytes. A traversing tail after the episode id still serves only that stored episode file, never another path. Closing the feed makes the previously working enclosure URL answer 404 while the media file stays on disk, and reopening the entity creates new episode ids whose URLs serve the same bytes.
